title: Matching one day of payments: ledger, provider report and bank statement
captions: Your ledger says three card payments succeeded today: A for ₹1,000, B for ₹500 and C for ₹200. It knows the gross amounts, but not the fees yet.
The provider's report lists what it put into this payout. It has A and B, with fees. It also has D, a payment your ledger never recorded. C is not there.
Match line by line on the payment id. A and B match. C exists only on your side. D exists only on the provider's side. Each gap is a break.

The payout is the sum of the net amounts, ₹1,764. It matches the bank deposit, and the trace id agrees. After you book the fees from the report, the items you matched, A and B, net to only ₹1,470. The extra ₹294 is D, which your ledger never recorded.
Every break goes to a queue with a type, an owner and an age. C is probably a timing gap, so you wait a day. D needs a check with the provider, then a new ledger entry. You never edit an old entry.
